A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IVEBench. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of four video-editing models, inference measurements and a human-alignment study in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: V2 reports evaluations of eight models, updated human-alignment results, annotator agreement and a new cross-metric correlation analysis.

M1.justification: The video and prompt construction pipeline, twelve evaluation metrics and human-weighted score aggregation remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–C. The newly evaluated editing models are comparators, not changes to IVEBench's method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 600-video benchmark, comprising 400 short and 200 long videos, with eight editing categories and 35 subcategories. No new dataset, domain or task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 expand the evaluated methods from InsV2V, AnyV2V, StableV2V and VACE to include Lucy-Edit-Dev, Omni-Video, ICVE and Ditto on both subsets. This substantially broadens the actual comparison set.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the reported human-validation sample from ten to 30 source videos, retaining three models and 30 annotators; this does not establish whether experiments were rerun. Appendix D specifies frame caps for new comparators: ICVE 81, Omni-Video 17 and Ditto 73. Existing benchmark splits and retained-model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix G and Figure A3 examine metric redundancy through a Spearman correlation matrix for eight metrics across the evaluated models. This adds a focused validation analysis; the existing qualitative cases and supplementary model analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 6.2 newly reports inter-rater reliability using Fleiss' kappa, obtaining 0.78, whereas v1 reports only human-metric correlations. Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 substantially expand performance and efficiency results while preserving all original-model values. New entries include Ditto's short/long compliance scores of 0.49/0.48 and Lucy-Edit-Dev's 1.52/2.23 seconds per frame under their respective settings. All twelve Table 4 correlations change alongside the revised study description, such as SC from 0.9583 to 0.9536. Kappa and the Figure A3 correlations are also new results.

T1.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same trajectory similarity, Hungarian matching, motion-fidelity equations and weighted scoring formulation. No formal assumptions, proofs or mathematical definitions are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a diverse instruction-guided editing benchmark, comprehensive task coverage and twelve human-aligned metrics. The added abstract promise of public resources repeats an existing commitment in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new correlations as evidence of metric independence and trade-offs, and kappa as evidence that annotator calibration aligned evaluation standards. The resolution discussion now includes 832×480 outputs. Most existing explanations of editing failures and scalability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Table 3 document frame limits, resolutions and resource measurements for the added models. V2 also specifies code release after acceptance and adds academic-research-use language. Existing resource links, retained-model configurations and failed-video lists remain unchanged; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Related work adds Ditto, Lucy-Edit, ICVE, Omni-Video, UniVideo and InstructX, including discussion of unified MLLM/video-generation architectures. V2 also adds statistical references and explicitly attributes four metrics to VBench. Its central positioning against existing editing benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local revisions expand related work and results discussion, add limitation, ethics and reproducibility statements, and update author contribution/contact information. The new Appendix G shifts the unchanged LLM-use statement to Appendix H.

P2.justification: The document receives a comprehensive visual redesign, including the title page, headers, typography, captions and spacing. Tables 2–3 expand, Figure 4 is redrawn for eight models with revised legends and axis ordering, and Figure A3 adds a heatmap. Existing qualitative figures are retained and reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a more informative comparison of editing capabilities and computational costs through additional model families, and strengthens reported human validation with 30 rather than ten videos and kappa of 0.78. The net gain is limited: heterogeneous frame caps constrain direct model comparisons, and Appendix G's pairwise correlations provide only limited support for its stronger claim of metric independence.
